stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core field of text-generation using transformer-based architectures.
The model is associated with Meta (formerly Facebook) and utilizes standard ML formats like safetensors.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native support for DFlash and image input via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: SpaceX intends to invest up to $100 billion in massive Louisiana spaceport
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: SpaceX plans a massive investment of up to $100 billion in a new spaceport located in Louisiana.
The project is described as being of unprecedented scale and significance.
This signals a major expansion and commitment by SpaceX to large-scale infrastructure development in the aerospace sector.

stories.title: New bootloader lets you take the "Meta" out of the original Meta Quest
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A new bootloader exploit allows users to bypass Meta's controls on the original Meta Quest.
The vulnerability enables privilege escalation, granting users 'full control' over the device.
This effectively frees the headset from mandatory reliance on Meta's servers and applications.

stories.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
stories.author: Matthias Bethge
bullet_points: Introduction of LAION-BVD, a massive open-source video dataset for multimodal AI training.
The dataset comprises 80 million videos totaling 10 million hours, sourced from CommonCrawl.
It is specifically designed to facilitate multimodal pre-training across video, audio, and image modalities using synthetic captioning.

stories.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
stories.author: Matthias Bethge
bullet_points: Introduction of LAION-BVD, a massive, open-source video dataset designed for multimodal learning.
The dataset comprises 80 million videos totaling 10 million hours, sourced from CommonCrawl.
It supports multimodal pre-training across video, audio, and image modalities, with synthetic caption generation used for training.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes common ML frameworks and formats like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for autonomous agents.
The model is designed for multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance, specifically on the Aider polyglot benchmark, shows up to a 90% speed increase.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, emphasizing privacy.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI inference speed.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: Bill Gates is deeply worried about AI, and he’s no longer staying quiet
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Bill Gates, previously an AI optimist, has shifted to a deeply pessimistic view regarding AI's future impact.
The shift in perspective is detailed in a substantial, nearly 6,000-word essay published by Gates.
This marks a significant public commentary from a major tech figure on the societal risks of artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Lab supply companies have been selling antibodies using manipulated images
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Lab supply companies are reportedly selling antibodies that utilize manipulated images.
The extent of image manipulation is described as widespread, suggesting systemic issues in the industry.
The quality of the manipulation is severe enough that it could warrant the retraction of scientific papers.

stories.title: Reading Is Not Using: Retrieval, Judgment, and the Design of AI Financial Research Workflows
stories.author: Zhizhe Liu
bullet_points: Identifies a critical 'retrieval-integration gap' in how LLMs are used for financial analysis.
Current evaluation methods for AI analysts focus too much on information retrieval rather than the quality of subsequent judgment.
Research demonstrates that the influence of specific financial disclosures changes significantly based on the volume of unrelated context provided to the LLM.

stories.title: What FID Hides: Detecting, Ranking, and Diagnosing Deviations in Generative Evaluation
stories.author: Hao Chen
bullet_points: The paper critiques the limitations of standard generative model evaluation metrics like FID and KID.
It highlights that FID's reliance on first-two-moment statistics can mask significant distributional differences in generated samples.
The research proposes methods for better detecting, ranking, and diagnosing deviations in generative model performance beyond simple scalar scores.

stories.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
stories.author: Lei Wu
bullet_points: The study identifies 'Effective Learning Rate' (ELR) as the primary factor governing loss dynamics in language model pretraining.
ELR, defined by the ratio of learning rate (LR) and parameter norm, dictates loss trajectories, causing them to collapse when matched.
The findings are robust, showing consistent results across various optimizers, architectures, datasets, and model scales.

stories.title: Z.ai confirms Ox Alpha is a new GLM-series model and will release its weights
stories.author: garo-pro
bullet_points: Z.ai has confirmed that Ox Alpha is a new model belonging to the GLM-series.
The company plans to release the weights for this new model.
This announcement signals further development and open-sourcing within the GLM model ecosystem.

stories.title: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra
stories.author: interpol_p
bullet_points: Apple has announced the introduction of new high-performance chips, specifically the M6 and M5 Ultra.
The M5 Ultra is highlighted as Apple's most powerful chip to date, indicating a significant leap in processing capability.
The news is covered by major tech publications, suggesting high industry relevance regarding Apple's silicon roadmap.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It strengthens Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon users.

stories.title: IBM's new Granite 4.2 models ride the wave of interest in local LLMs
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: IBM has released new Granite 4.2 language models.
The models are specifically tailored for enterprise deployment.
A key focus of the new models is enhancing agentic capabilities.

stories.title: The world's busiest spaceport is about to get a lot quieter, at least for now
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX is planning to launch its Starship vehicle from a Florida spaceport.
The target launch timeframe is ambitious, with a potential goal for the end of the year.
However, the article suggests a more realistic timeline for Starship deployment is closer to 2027.

stories.title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL
stories.author: Zihe Huang
bullet_points: Introduces SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization, designed to address computational costs in group-relative reinforcement learning for long, variable tool-use trajectories.
Addresses a limitation in Single-stream Policy Optimization (SPO) where trajectory centering fails to properly center the token-weighted actor loss.
The core technical contribution involves standardizing the optimization process to fix the mismatch between trajectory centering and the token-weighted quantity consumed by the actor.

stories.title: FedV-KGQA: Multi-Hop Question Answering over Vertically Partitioned Knowledge Graphs
stories.author: Oshani Seneviratne
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of multi-hop Question Answering (QA) when knowledge graphs are vertically partitioned across different organizations.
Proposes FedV-KGQA, a framework designed to enable reasoning across data silos while respecting data sovereignty.
The core technical innovation involves allowing organizations to share entities but maintain ownership over disjoint sets of relations.

stories.title: Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge for LLM-Based Knowledge Graph QA
stories.author: Emanuel Kitzelmann
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of LLM grounding in Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA).
Compares two existing methods: brittle full semantic parsing (e.g., SPARQL) versus less formally guaranteed LLM reasoning.
Proposes a new approach focusing on Constrained Entity Selection under Partial Knowledge to improve robustness.

stories.title: Strictly Causal Streaming Video Anomaly Detection with a Theoretically-Grounded State-Space Core
stories.author: Yogesh Kumar
bullet_points: Introduces a strictly causal streaming video anomaly detector utilizing state-space models (SSMs).
Addresses limitations of prior work by achieving O(1) time and memory per incoming frame update.
Focuses on theoretical grounding and edge hardware efficiency, moving beyond simple GPU throughput benchmarks.

stories.title: Automatic Model Card Generation Using an LLM
stories.author: Cor-Paul Bezemer
bullet_points: Addresses the lack of standardization and availability of Model Cards for ML models.
Introduces MCTidy, an LLM-based approach designed to reorganize existing model cards into a standardized template.
Aims to improve transparency, usability, and comparability across different machine learning models.

stories.title: StarHarness: Evolving Harnesses with Stratified Search for Enterprise Environments
stories.author: Sagar Davasam
bullet_points: StarHarness is a new framework designed to evolve agent harnesses for specific enterprise environments.
It allows for customization of agent components (prompts, tools, skills, subagent structure) without altering the core model weights.
The framework uses stratified search and task separation to efficiently manage the evolution and evaluation process.

stories.title: BioKERN: Biological Kernel Regularization for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Neighborhood Retrieval
stories.author: Betul Orcan-Ekmekci
bullet_points: Introduces BioKERN, a new multimodal spatial representation-learning framework.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods that focus only on instance-level matching in histology-transcriptomics data.
Incorporates biological structure as an explicit, learnable inductive bias to preserve neighborhood relationships.

stories.title: A Geometric Theory of Robust Fairness Audits
stories.author: Binita Maity
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of robustness in neighborhood-based fairness audits used in machine learning.
These audits are sensitive to small feature space perturbations, which can change local neighborhoods and alter fairness assessments.
The authors introduce a geometric framework to analyze and improve the robustness of these fairness auditing procedures.

stories.title: LION: A Clifford Neural Paradigm for Multimodal-Attributed Graph Learning
stories.author: Guoren Wang
bullet_points: The research introduces LION, a new Clifford Neural Paradigm designed for Multimodal-Attributed Graph Learning.
The trend in Graph ML is shifting towards multimodal-attributed graphs to better enhance data representation for complex downstream tasks.
Current neural paradigms are limited by neglecting context during modality alignment, which LION aims to address.

stories.title: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: BrowserForge addresses the data scarcity problem for training web agents that operate on rendered pixels, bypassing the limitations of HTML/accessibility tree parsing.
The core challenge identified is generating large volumes of high-quality interaction trajectories needed to train these pixel-based web agents.
The work suggests a method (Parallel Browser Sandboxes) to scale data generation beyond the small, fixed datasets currently available.

stories.title: Reading Is Not Using: Retrieval, Judgment, and the Design of AI Financial Research Workflows
stories.author: Zhizhe Liu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a 'retrieval-integration gap' in AI financial research, noting that current LLM evaluations focus too much on information retrieval rather than how that information influences judgment.
The research investigates how the volume of unrelated context (from 2k to 128k tokens) affects the influence of specific risk disclosures on AI analysis.
This work is highly relevant to the practical deployment and trustworthiness of LLMs used as AI analysts in the high-stakes financial sector.

stories.title: Linear Probing Provides Robust and Efficient Detection of Machine-Generated Text
stories.author: Elena Simperl
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need to distinguish machine-generated text (MGT) from human-written text (HWT) due to misuse concerns.
The study demonstrates that simple linear probes can effectively detect MGT, outperforming many complex supervised detectors.
A key finding is that MGT and HWT latent representations exhibit linearity, allowing for highly sample-efficient detection methods.

stories.title: ExpConCAD: Experience-Guided Text-to-CAD Generation from Shape Descriptions with Implicit Spatial Constraints
stories.author: See-Kiong Ng
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge in Text-to-CAD generation: underspecified natural language descriptions lacking necessary spatial constraints.
Proposes 'ExpConCAD,' a method that infers missing spatial constraints by leveraging underlying construction structure and reusable design experience.
Focuses on moving Text-to-CAD from simple generation to producing valid, executable CAD programs suitable for real-world engineering.

stories.title: The RAT: A Unified Bayesian Model for RAG Evaluation
stories.author: Jan Deriu
bullet_points: Introduces 'The RAT,' a unified Bayesian model specifically designed for evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
The framework jointly models retrieval success, answer correctness, and abstention behavior, addressing complex pipeline interactions.
It provides a granular view of task success by factorizing the model according to the information flow within the RAG pipeline.

stories.title: SkillForge: Evolving Verifiable Skills for Reinforcement Learning Agents
stories.author: Xiangxiang Chu
bullet_points: SkillForge addresses a limitation in RL agents by introducing verifiable skills for complex decision-making.
Existing skill-based RL methods (like SkillRL) lack verification, treating the skill bank as a simple, append-only repository.
The research focuses on enabling RL agents to accumulate and reuse knowledge effectively across different task episodes.

stories.title: The Model Scored 30%. The Harness Scored 100%. Which One Did You Benchmark?
stories.author: p0rt
bullet_points: The article discusses a benchmarking discrepancy where a 'harness' achieved 100% performance while a 'model' only scored 30% on a specific dataset.
A key finding is that four harnesses improved performance from 13% to 100% without modifying model weights.
The context suggests an investigation into the impact of integrating these harnesses within a training loop, potentially highlighting evaluation methodology issues.
